html.body: Date: 2025-04-15 REMARKSClaims 1-20 are pending in the current application. Claims 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, and 19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over US 2019/0258263 to Wendel in view of US 2022/0221867 to Taveira. Claims 2, 9, and 16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Wendel in view of Taveira and US 2019/0176837 to Williams.Reconsideration is respectfully requested in view of the remarks and amendments submitted herewith.Allowable Subject Matter Applicant thankfully acknowledges the Examiner's indication that claims 4, 6-7, 11, 13- 14, 18, and 20 include patentable subject matter which would be allowable upon being rewritten in independent form.Amendments to the Claims Claims 1, 6, and 7 have been amended as shown herein. Claims 5 and 8-20 have been canceled.Independent claim 1 has been amended to recite that the controller is configured to:acquire, by the acquisition interface, passenger information including posture information of a passenger in the cabin; and provide, by the output interface based on the travel event information, a notification that is different depending on the posture information, in the cabin.Claim 6 has been amended to recite the features of independent claim 1 and the features of intervening dependent claim 5 except replacing that "the second condition is a condition indicating that a predetermined number or more passengers are elderly or children" with "the condition is a condition indicating that a predetermined number or more passengers satisfy a predetermined characteristic of the passengers".Claim 7 has been amended to recite the features of independent claim 1 and to replace "the output interface is configured to be capable of providing multiple patterns of notifications that are different depending on the boarding position of the passenger" with "the output interface is configured to be capable of providing multiple patterns of notifications that are different depending on the passenger information".Support for these amendments may be found in the specification, figures and claims as originally filed. No subject matter has been disclaimed and the amendment of certain claims is not to be construed as a dedication to the public of any of the subject matter of the claims as previously presented. It is believed that no new matter has been entered through these amendments and entry is respectfully requested.Summary of Examiner Interview Cesare A. Sclafani thanks Examiner Thomas McCormack for the telephonic interview of April 9, 2025. The specification, claims and drawings of the instant application were discussed in view of the cited prior art. A tentative agreement was reached regarding the proposed claim amendments, which are formally presented herein, overcoming the current rejections. However, the Examiner indicated that an updated search and consideration would be required.Entry of this statement of substance of interview is requested as this statement is in compliance with 37 C.F.R. §1.133.Rejections under 35 U.S.C. .103 As noted hereinabove, claims 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, and 19 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Wendel in view of Taveira, and claims 2, 9, and 16 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Wendel in view of Taveira and Williams. The rejections are respectfully traversed.The rationale to support a conclusion that the claim would have been obvious is that all the claimed elements were known in the prior art and one skilled in the art could have combined the elements as claimed by known methods with no change in their respective functions, and the combination yielded nothing more than predictable results to one of ordinary skill in the art. KSR, 550 U.S. at 416, 82 USPQ2d at 1395; Sakraida v. AG Pro, Inc., 425 U.S. 273, 282, 189 USPQ 449, 453 (1976); Anderson's-Black Rock, Inc. v. Pavement Salvage Co., 396 U.S. 57, 62- 63, 163 USPQ 673, 675 (1969); Great At. & P. Tea Co. v. Supermarket Equip. Corp., 340 U.S.147, 152, 87 USPQ 303, 306 (1950). Further, "a prior art reference must be considered in its entirety, i.e., as a whole, including portions that would lead away from the claimed invention." W.L. Gore & Assoc., Inc. v. Garlock, Inc., 721 F.2d 1540, 220 USPQ 303 (Fed. Cir. 1983), cert.denied, 469 U.S. 851 (1984).As tentatively agreed during the telephone interview, Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of Wendel, Taveira, and Williams fails to expressly or inherently disclose or make obvious the features of amended independent claim 1. Specifically, the combination of Wendel, Taveira, and Williams fails to expressly or inherently disclose or make obvious the features of amended independent claim 1 regarding that the controller is configured to: acquire, by the acquisition interface, passenger information including posture information of a passenger in the cabin; and provide, by the output interface based on the travel event information, a notification that is different depending on the posture information, in the cabin.As tentatively agreed during the telephone interview, Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of Wendel, Taveira, and Williams fails to expressly or inherently disclose or make obvious the features of amended independent claim 6. Specifically, the combination of Wendel, Taveira, and Williams fails to expressly or inherently disclose or make obvious the features of amended independent claim 6 regarding that the condition is a condition indicating that a predetermined number or more passengers satisfy a predetermined characteristic of the passengers.As tentatively agreed during the telephone interview, Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of Wendel, Taveira, and Williams fails to expressly or inherently disclose or make obvious the features of amended independent claim 7. Specifically, the combination of Wendel, Taveira, and Williams fails to expressly or inherently disclose or make obvious the features of amended independent claim 7 regarding that the output interface is configured to be capable of providing multiple patterns of notifications that are different depending on the boarding position of the passenger information.Based on the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 1, 6, and 7, and claims that depend thereon, can no longer be rejected as obvious over Wendel in view Taveira and Williams. Withdrawal of the rejections and a timely notice of allowance are respectfully requested.Conclusion In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned to resolve efficiently any formal matters or to discuss any aspects of the application or of this response.Otherwise, early notification of allowable subject matter is respectfully requested.No additional fees are believed to be due. However, the Director is hereby authorized to charge all required fees (including any extension of time fees) and to credit any overpayment of fees in this and any concurrent or future correspondence to Deposit Account No. 041133.Respectfully submitted, /Cesare A.
